title: Security

## Reporting a vulnerability

Report security bugs to
**[shain.singh@owasp.org](mailto:shain.singh@owasp.org)** or through
GitHub's private vulnerability reporting:
[Report a vulnerability](https://github.com/shsingh/agentpcap/security/advisories/new).
Never open a public issue for an unreported vulnerability. Reports may
go encrypted to the project's
[OpenPGP key](https://github.com/shsingh.gpg)
(`9CB1781DC2BB28D37A0155DCAAF8226F3F4C1712`); advisory text and key
material live in [SECURITY.md](https://github.com/shsingh/agentpcap/blob/main/SECURITY.md).

## What counts as a security bug here

- **Read-only invariant regression** — any path that writes to traffic,
  injects, or terminates connections. The tap changes no path.
- **Ledger chain integrity** — appends without the `prev` hash, rewrites
  of prior segments, or access-log under-capture.
- **eBPF surface regression** — unpinned probe bytecode, capability
  escalation beyond the documented set.
- **Capture-scope regression** — the tap observing outside its
  configured scope: hosts, transports, or content classes beyond the
  documented tool message.
- **Classification misstatement** — verdicts or evidence that misstate
  an observation.

## Authorised use

The tap observes estates the operator owns or is authorised to
observe: its own hosts, its own clusters, and lab fleets built for
evaluation. Australian users: the Cyber Security Act 2024 (Cth) and
Criminal Code Act 1995 (Cth) Div 474 apply; other jurisdictions carry
their own equivalents.

## Repository hygiene

Secret scanning and push protection stay on; every commit carries a
signature; Dependency Review checks licence and vulnerability deltas on
every pull request.
